page: Amazon Web Services c7i.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, compute-optimized server featuring 192 vCPUs and 96 physical cores powered by Intel Xeon 8488C processors running at 3.2 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance provides dedicated CPU allocation with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 384.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. The server does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, but it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark data highlights the multi-core capabilities of this bare-metal configuration. In multi-core CPU performance tests, such as stress-ng and PassMark CPU, the server ranks in the top 10% tier. It also achieves top-tier status in memory bandwidth read-only tests for both small and large blocks, as well as in specialized workloads like software compilation, ray tracing, image processing, and text processing. Single-core performance, measured by stress-ng, falls in the middle 50% tier, indicating that the server's strength lies in parallelized execution rather than single-threaded speed.

The c7i.metal-48xl offers high compute density and memory bandwidth, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for highly parallelized workloads that do not require local storage or GPU acceleration. The absence of local storage means all storage operations must rely on network-attached options, which is a key architectural tradeoff. Given its top-tier multi-core performance, high-speed DDR5 memory, and advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and AMX, this server is suited for heavy multi-threaded tasks, including software compilation, static web serving, Redis databases, and CPU-based LLM inference.
